title: Creating, inserting, and removing elements
learningObjectives: Explain creating, inserting, and removing elements and update browser documents with safe DOM and event patterns.

understand.concept: DOM methods such as createElement(), append(), prepend(), before(), after(), replaceWith(), and remove() create and change document nodes. Use textContent for untrusted text and set attributes through appropriate DOM APIs. Avoid building HTML strings from untrusted input.
understand.whyItMatters: Creating nodes through DOM methods keeps data separate from markup and reduces injection risks. It also makes the structure of generated content easier to inspect.
understand.analogy: DOM methods are like assembling a page from labelled building blocks rather than asking the browser to interpret a handwritten markup string.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual DOM, event, and security behaviour follows browser platform rules.

explain.narrative: The script creates an li element, sets its text, and appends it to the list.

examples.explanation: The script creates an li element, sets its text, and appends it to the list.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser page updates in response to safe DOM operations or user events.

practise.guidedTask: Create three list items from an array of topic names using createElement and append. Add a button that removes one item.
practise.independentTask: Build a small interactive component using DOM methods and event listeners. Handle missing elements and user input safely.
hints: Keep event handlers focused and avoid duplicate listeners.
Use event delegation for suitable dynamic lists.

questions.prompt: Which method creates a new HTML element node?
questions.explanation: createElement() creates an element node with the specified tag name.

questions.prompt: What is a safe DOM update pattern for user-provided text?
options: Set textContent on an existing element
Build an HTML string and assign it to innerHTML
questions.answer: Set textContent on an existing element
questions.explanation: textContent treats the value as text and avoids parsing untrusted markup.
